collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two villagers argue whether caring for the island is a duty, a faith or just good sense: argue on, or plant a tree together.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) says the island is alive, that spirits look after its forests and reefs, and that caring for it is a sacred duty. (friend) says it is rocks and soil and water, and caring for it is plain common sense. They have been arguing about it on the same log for an hour. They both agree it needs caring for. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They argue until dark. (subject) talks about the night the forest went silent before the storm. (friend) talks about how the soil washes away when the trees are gone. Neither of them changes the other's mind. They walk home together, still arguing, and both of them pick up a piece of rubbish on the path.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) suggests they stop arguing and plant something. They plant a young breadfruit tree on the bare slope behind the village. (subject) says a few words to the spirits over it. (friend) waters it. It grows well, and they never agree on why.
